narrative:
Your law school application was denied because the model estimated a 74.5% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt if admitted. That is a high-risk prediction, not a certainty, but it was strong enough to drive the rejection.

The most influential factor was your class standing in the third year. You were in the lowest decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile; this pushed the prediction toward bar failure. The second most important factor was your first-year class standing, also the lowest decile against an accepted-student average near the sixth decile, which again pushed toward failure. Third, your part-time study plan mattered: most accepted students intended to study full-time, and your part-time status increased the failure risk in the model. Gender and race were not used.

To improve a future application, focus on raising your academic standing, especially in advanced coursework, and seek academic advising for a concrete improvement plan. If possible, plan for full-time study or reduce outside work demands during law school, and consider strengthening your LSAT and undergraduate GPA profile. Addressing these areas would make the next application more competitive and reduce the predicted bar-exam risk.
